title: Neuralink Gets FDA Green Light for LINK, the First U.S. Pivotal Brain Implant Trial
yt_title: Neuralink's Brain Chip Gets FDA Go for First U.S. Pivotal Trial | ALS & the N1 Implant
yt_description:
The FDA has approved Neuralink's LINK study, which the company calls the first U.S. pivotal trial of an implantable brain-computer interface. Adults with ALS could control computers and phones just by thinking, using the wireless N1 implant. Here's how it works, what the trial measures, and what it can't do.

script: Welcome to IT News, AI News! Today, a brain chip just walked through a very big door. Neuralink says the U S Food and Drug Administration approved its first pivotal trial. The study is called LINK. Pivotal means this is the big one. It is the kind of trial that can collect the evidence for a future market approval. Neuralink calls it the first pivotal trial of an implantable brain computer interface in the United States. The device is the N one implant. It sits in the skull, with no wires sticking out and no external battery. It charges wirelessly, right through the scalp. Like your phone on a pad, but way more personal. A surgical robot called R one places tiny, flexible threads into the brain. Steady hands, literally made of metal. The trial is for adults with A L S, the disease that slowly takes away movement, and often speech. The goal: control a computer, a phone, or a cursor, just by thinking about moving your hand. The study will measure safety, how well it works, and whether it really helps people live more independently. Neuralink says it builds on more than thirty people already implanted in early studies. Those volunteers are in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, with thousands of hours of use. Early users have browsed the web, sent messages, played video games, and even written code. With their minds! One reported plan has follow up visits lasting up to twenty four months after the implant. But careful: the chip does not cure A L S, and it does not bring back movement or natural speech. It is still an investigational device. Passing this trial does not guarantee approval. The FDA gets the final word. So, is mind control for your laptop almost here? Tell us in the comments! Full story on itnewsainews dot xpigeon dot net.
